questions.q: Match each renal compartment with its share of renal mass — 1) Tubular/interstitium 2) Glomerular 3) Vascular … A) 10% B) 85% C) 5%
questions.exp: Renal compartments: tubular/interstitium 85%, glomerular 10%, vascular 5%. (Book p717)

questions.q: Fill up: The bladder derives from the cloaca (primitive rectum) except its trigone, which comes from the ______ (mesodermal).
questions.exp: Bladder from cloaca (primitive rectum) except the trigone, which is mesonephric duct (mesodermal). (Book p717)

questions.q: All of the following urethral segments and their origins are correctly paired EXCEPT:
opts: Prostatic urethra up to the ejaculatory duct opening: pelvic part of definitive UG sinus
Prostatic urethra up to the ejaculatory duct opening: vesico-ureteric canal
Membranous and remaining prostatic urethra: pelvic part of definitive UG sinus
Spongy urethra: cephalic part of UG sinus
questions.exp: The prostatic urethra up to the ejaculatory duct opening is the vesico-ureteric canal; the pelvic part of the definitive UG sinus gives the membranous and remaining prostatic urethra, and the cephalic part gives the spongy urethra. (Book p717)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the anal canal origin is TRUE?
opts: Up to the pectinate line it is cloacal, below the pectinate line it is the anal pit
Below the pectinate line it is cloacal
The whole canal is derived from the anal pit
The whole canal is derived from the cloaca
questions.exp: Anal canal: up to the pectinate line from cloaca, below the pectinate line from the anal pit. (Book p717)

questions.q: The prostate develops from the:
questions.exp: Prostate arises from the primitive urogenital sinus (UG sinus). (Book p717)

questions.q: The excretory part of the kidney originates from the:
opts: Nephrogenic cord, derived from the urogenital ridge
questions.exp: Excretory part origin: nephrogenic cord, derived from the urogenital ridge (the collecting part is the ureteric-bud side). (Book p717)

questions.q: Match each excretory-part entry with its description — 1) Renal corpuscle 2) Pars convoluta (S1+S3) 3) Pars recta (S3) … A) Proximal straight tubule B) Glomerulus + Bowman's capsule C) Proximal convoluted tubule
questions.exp: 1 = glomerulus + Bowman's capsule = renal corpuscle; 2 = PCT (pars convoluta) S1+S3; 3 = proximal straight tubule (pars recta) S3. (Book p717)

questions.q: Fill up: In the numbered excretory-part list, the thin ascending limb of the loop of Henle carries segment number ______.
questions.exp: Segment 4 = thin descending limb, 5 = thin ascending limb of the loop of Henle. (Book p717)

questions.q: All of the following belong to the distal tubule (DT) group EXCEPT:
opts: Thin ascending limb of loop of Henle
questions.exp: DT group = segments 6 (thick ascending/distal straight), 7 (DCT) and 8 (macula densa); the thin ascending limb (5) belongs to the intermediate tubule. (Book p717)

questions.q: Fill up: The pars recta of the proximal tubule corresponds to segment ______ of the proximal tubule.
questions.exp: Pars convoluta spans S1+S3 while pars recta is S3. (Book p717)

questions.q: Segment 6 of the excretory part is the:
opts: Thick ascending limb of loop of Henle (distal straight tubule)
Thin ascending limb of loop of Henle
questions.exp: Segment 6 = thick ascending limb of loop of Henle, also called the distal straight tubule. (Book p717)

questions.q: The last numbered segment (8) of the excretory part is the:
questions.exp: The excretory list ends: 7 distal convoluted tubule, 8 macula densa. (Book p717)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the excretory part is TRUE?
opts: It is listed as eight segments ending with the macula densa
It is listed as twelve segments ending with the inner medullary collecting duct
The proximal tubule group comprises segments 4 and 5
questions.exp: The excretory part lists 8 segments (renal corpuscle to macula densa); the 9-12 numbering belongs to the collecting part. (Book p717)

questions.q: Match each collecting-part segment with its number — 1) Connecting tubule 2) Cortical collecting duct 3) Inner medullary collecting duct … A) 12 B) 9 C) 10
questions.exp: 9 = connecting tubule (CT), 10 = cortical collecting duct, 11 = outer medullary collecting duct, 12 = inner medullary collecting duct. (Book p718)

questions.q: Fill up: The collecting part originates from the epithelium of the ______.
questions.exp: Collecting part origin: epithelium of ureteric bud, derived from mesonephric duct, derived from intermediate mesoderm. (Book p718)

questions.q: Following the origin chain of the collecting part (ureteric bud epithelium → mesonephric duct), the final embryonic source is the:
questions.exp: Ureteric bud epithelium derives from the mesonephric duct, which derives from intermediate mesoderm. (Book p718)

questions.q: The collecting part (CP) bracket includes all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: CP spans CT, CD, ureter, pelvis and calyces; the proximal convoluted tubule is excretory, not collecting. (Book p718)

questions.q: Cortical (short-looped) nephrons make up what proportion of all nephrons?
questions.exp: Cortical nephrons 85%, juxtamedullary (long-looped) 15%. (Book p718)

questions.q: Match each nephron type with its loop tip and concentrating role — 1) Cortical nephron 2) Juxtamedullary nephron … A) Loop tip inside inner medulla; major role in urine concentration B) Loop tip till the junction of outer and inner medulla; lesser role
opts: Both end at the outer medulla
questions.exp: Cortical (short-looped): tip till junction of outer and inner medulla, lesser role; juxtamedullary (long-looped): tip inside inner medulla, major role. (Book p718)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about nephron types is TRUE?
opts: Juxtamedullary nephrons are long-looped and form 15% of nephrons
Juxtamedullary nephrons are short-looped and form 85%
Cortical nephrons have the major role in urine concentration
Cortical nephron loops reach inside the inner medulla
questions.exp: Juxtamedullary nephrons are the long-looped 15% with the major concentrating role; cortical are the short-looped 85%. (Book p718)

questions.q: Match each renal-failure pattern with its category — 1) Hours to days 2) Days to weeks 3) Falling number of functional nephrons … A) Rapidly progressive renal failure B) Acute kidney injury C) CKD
questions.exp: Non-CKD renal failure over hours to days = AKI; over days to weeks = rapidly progressive renal failure; CKD = falling number of functional nephrons. (Book p718)

questions.q: Fill up: The m/c cause of acute tubular necrosis / tubular injury is ______.
questions.exp: ATN/tubular injury: m/c cause ischemia; m/c site PST (proximal straight tubule). (Book p718)

questions.q: The m/c site of acute tubular injury is the:
questions.exp: m/c site of ATN = PST (proximal straight tubule). (Book p718)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about acute interstitial nephritis is TRUE?
opts: It is caused mainly by ischemia
It is a post-renal cause of failure
questions.exp: Acute interstitial nephritis is a hypersensitivity reaction, distinct from ischemic ATN. (Book p718)

questions.q: In the renal-failure tree, the 'Causes outside Kidney' branch splits into:
questions.exp: Causes outside the kidney are pre-renal and post-renal; tubulointerstitial causes belong to the AKI (inside-kidney) arm. (Book p718)

questions.q: The two tubulointerstitial causes of AKI in the book's tree are:
opts: Acute tubular necrosis/tubular injury and acute interstitial nephritis
CKD and rapidly progressive renal failure
questions.exp: AKI tubulointerstitial causes: ATN/tubular injury and acute interstitial nephritis. (Book p718)

questions.q: The PCT maximally reabsorbs all of the following ions EXCEPT:
questions.exp: PCT gives maximum reabsorption of all ions except Mg2+ (which is maximally absorbed in the thick ascending loop). (Book p719)

questions.q: Match each PCT Na+-dependent symporter with its substrate — 1) Na+-dependent amino acid transporter 2) SGLT-2 3) Na+-dependent phosphate transporter type II … A) Glucose B) Amino acids C) Phosphate
questions.exp: Symporters: amino acid transporter (AA), SGLT-2 (glucose), phosphate transporter type II (phosphate). (Book p719)

questions.q: The antiport listed under PCT secondary active transport is the:
questions.exp: PCT antiport = Na+-H+ antiport. (Book p719)

questions.q: Fill up: Passive transport in the PCT is paracellular (PPT) and occurs on the membrane between ______.
questions.exp: Passive transport = paracellular transport (PPT) on the membrane between two cells. (Book p719)

questions.q: Fill up: Phosphorus is handled only in the kidney; PCT damage causes phosphorus loss leading to ______.
questions.exp: Phosphorus only handled in kidney; PCT damage → phosphorus loss → rickets. (Book p719)

questions.q: Match each carbonic anhydrase type with its location in the PCT diagram — 1) Type II 2) Type IV … A) Luminal side, splitting H2CO3 into H2O + CO2 B) Intracellular, forming H2CO3 from H2O + CO2
opts: Both act on the luminal membrane
questions.exp: Carbonic anhydrase type II is intracellular (H2O+CO2→H2CO3→H++HCO3-); type IV is luminal (H2CO3→H2O+CO2). (Book p719)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about magnesium handling is TRUE?
opts: Mg2+ is maximally absorbed in the thick ascending loop of Henle
Mg2+ is maximally absorbed in the PCT
Mg2+ is maximally absorbed in the cortical collecting duct
questions.exp: Note: Mg2+ maximally absorbed in the thick ascending loop of Henle (hence PCT reabsorbs all ions except Mg2+). (Book p719)

questions.q: In the PCT diagram, the HCO3- generated intracellularly by carbonic anhydrase type II exits across the:
questions.exp: Intracellular H2CO3 splits to H+ (recycled luminally) and HCO3-, which leaves via the basolateral membrane. (Book p719)

questions.q: Global dysfunction of the PCT is also known as:
opts: Fanconi syndrome / type-2 RTA / proximal RTA
questions.exp: Global PCT dysfunction = Fanconi syndrome = type-2 RTA = proximal RTA. (Book p720)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Fanconi syndrome aetiology is TRUE?
questions.exp: The tree shows inherited >> acquired for global PCT dysfunction. (Book p720)

questions.q: Match each age group with its m/c cause of Fanconi syndrome — 1) Children 2) Adolescents 3) Adults 4) Elderly … A) Drugs B) Cystinosis C) Multiple myeloma D) Wilson's disease
questions.exp: m/c causes: children = cystinosis, adolescents = Wilson's disease, adults = drugs, elderly = multiple myeloma. (Book p720)

questions.q: Fill up: Cystinosis, the m/c cause of Fanconi syndrome in children, is inherited in an autosomal ______ manner.
questions.exp: Cystinosis: m/c in children, autosomal recessive. (Book p720)

questions.q: All of the following drugs are listed causes of Fanconi syndrome EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Drug causes: ifosfamide, tenofovir, valproate, outdated tetracycline and cisplatin; ceftriaxone is not listed. (Book p720)

questions.q: Fill up: Acetazolamide and ______ cause acidosis without generalized PCT dysfunction by inhibiting HCO3- reabsorption.
questions.exp: Note: acetazolamide and topiramate inhibit HCO3- reabsorption, causing acidosis without generalized PCT dysfunction. (Book p720)

questions.q: The m/c cause of Fanconi syndrome in the elderly is:
questions.exp: Multiple myeloma is the m/c cause in the elderly. (Book p720)

questions.q: Match each Fanconi cardinal loss with its consequence — 1) Phosphorus loss 2) HCO3- loss 3) Amino-acid loss … A) Wasting / growth retardation B) Renal rickets C) Normal anion gap metabolic acidosis
questions.exp: Phosphorus loss → renal rickets; HCO3- loss → NAGMA; AA loss → wasting/growth retardation. (Book p720)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Fanconi syndrome is TRUE?
opts: RFT is normal with very minimal proteinuria, so there is no risk of CKD
RFT is deranged with heavy proteinuria
It carries a high risk of progression to CKD
questions.exp: Cardinal feature 2: normal RFT, very minimal proteinuria → no risk for CKD. (Book p720)

questions.q: The glycosuria seen in Fanconi syndrome is characteristically:
questions.exp: Cardinal feature 3: euglycemic glycosuria (glucose lost despite normal blood sugar). (Book p720)

questions.q: The anion gap in the NAGMA of Fanconi syndrome is:
questions.exp: NAGMA with anion gap 8–12 meq/; 16–18 mEq is the HCO3- level (no significant acidosis). (Book p720)

questions.q: Fill up: The normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis of Fanconi syndrome is also called hyperchloremic ______.
questions.exp: NAGMA aka hyperchloremic acidosis. (Book p720)

questions.q: In Fanconi syndrome the serum HCO3- level (no significant acidosis) is:
questions.exp: No significant acidosis: HCO3- 16–18 mEq; urine acidification remains normal (intercalated cells) with urine pH 4–4.5. (Book p720)

questions.q: Fill up: Salt and water depletion in Fanconi syndrome triggers secondary RAAS activation and raised aldosterone, causing K+ wasting and ______.
questions.exp: Salt & water depletion → secondary RAAS → ↑ aldosterone → K+ wasting → hypokalemia. (Book p720)

questions.q: All of the following are 'other features' of Fanconi syndrome EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Other features: hypouricemia, hypocarnitinemia, polyuria, dehydration and minimal proteinuria — uric acid is low, not high. (Book p720)

questions.q: All of the following are cell types of the cortical collecting duct EXCEPT:
questions.exp: CCD cell types: P-cell, α-intercalated cells, β-1 cells and un-named cells; podocytes are glomerular. (Book p721)

questions.q: Fill up: In the P-cell, aldosterone induces AIP which positively stimulates the luminal ______ channel.
questions.exp: Aldosterone → aldosterone receptors → AIP (aldosterone inducing protein) → (+) ENaC on the luminal membrane. (Book p721)

questions.q: The aldosterone acting on the P-cell is secreted by the:
questions.exp: Zona glomerulosa → aldosterone → P-cell aldosterone receptors. (Book p721)

questions.q: Excess aldosterone produces all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Excess aldosterone → HTN, metabolic alkalosis and hypokalemia (the Conn's triad); hyperkalemia is the opposite. (Book p721)

questions.q: The triad of hypertension, metabolic alkalosis and hypokalemia from excess aldosterone defines:
questions.exp: Excess aldosterone → HTN + metabolic alkalosis + hypokalemia → Conn's syndrome. (Book p721)

questions.q: Besides ENaC, the luminal channels labelled in the P-cell diagram that secrete H+ and K+ are:
questions.exp: The P-cell diagram labels ROMK/SOMK secreting H+ + K+ at the luminal membrane. (Book p721)

questions.q: Fill up: Hypoaldosteronism is also called renal tubular acidosis type ______.
questions.exp: Hypoaldosteronism = RTA type IV (RTA-IV). (Book p721)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about RTA-IV is TRUE?
opts: It causes hyperkalemia disproportionate to the degree and duration of renal failure
It causes hypokalemia without renal failure
Potassium levels always match the degree of renal failure
It is caused by excess aldosterone
questions.exp: RTA-IV: hyperkalemia without renal failure, or hyperkalemia disproportionate to the degree and duration of renal failure. (Book p721)

questions.q: Match each true hypoaldosteronism subtype with its renin/aldosterone pattern — 1) Hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism 2) Hyper-reninemic hypoaldosteronism … A) ↑ Renin with ↓ Aldo B) ↓ Renin with ↓ Aldo
questions.exp: Hyporeninemic = ↓ renin ↓ aldo; hyper-reninemic = ↑ renin ↓ aldo. (Book p721)

questions.q: All of the following cause hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Hyporeninemic causes: NSAIDs, β-blockers, aliskiren (direct renin inhibitor) and diabetes mellitus; ACE inhibitors cause the hyper-reninemic form. (Book p721)

questions.q: All of the following cause hyper-reninemic hypoaldosteronism EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Hyper-reninemic causes: adrenal insufficiency (Addison's), drugs (ACEi, ARBs) and aldosterone synthase inhibitors (heparin, ketoconazole); NSAIDs give the hyporeninemic form. (Book p721)

questions.q: Match each acquired pseudo-hypoaldosteronism agent with its mechanism — 1) Spironolactone / eplerenone 2) Amiloride / triamterene 3) Trimethoprim … A) ENaC channel blockade B) Aldosterone receptor blockade C) Structure similar to triamterene
questions.exp: Spironolactone/eplerenone block aldosterone receptors; amiloride/triamterene block ENaC; trimethoprim resembles triamterene. (Book p721)

questions.q: Fill up: Inherited pseudo-hypoaldosteronism occurs as PHA type-1 and PHA type-______.
questions.exp: Inherited PHA: type-1 and type-2. (Book p721)

questions.q: All of the following are renin stimulators EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Renin stimulators: prostaglandins, β1-receptors and renal hypoperfusion; NSAIDs and β-blockers inhibit them (−). (Book p722)

questions.q: Match each intercalated cell with its luminal transporters — 1) α-1 cell 2) β-1 cell … A) Pendrin channel and anion exchanger B) H+-K+ ATPase and H+ ATPase
questions.exp: α-1 cell luminal: H+-K+ ATPase and H+ ATPase (with intracellular CA-II); β-1 cell luminal: pendrin channel, basolateral anion exchanger. (Book p722)

questions.q: Fill up: The carbonic anhydrase working inside the α-1 cell is type ______.
questions.exp: α-1 cell contains carbonic anhydrase-II (the PCT luminal enzyme is type IV). (Book p722)

questions.q: Fill up: The autosomal dominant inherited defect in type-1/distal RTA is a defect of the ______.
questions.exp: Inherited type-1 RTA: AD defect = anion exchanger defect; AR defect = H+ ATPase or H+/K+ ATPase defect. (Book p722)

questions.q: The autosomal recessive inherited form of distal RTA (H+ ATPase or H+/K+ ATPase defect) may present with:
questions.exp: AR defect (H+ ATPase or H+/K+ ATPase) may present with SNHL. (Book p722)

questions.q: The m/c acquired cause of type-1/distal RTA is:
questions.exp: Sjogren's syndrome is the m/c acquired cause; amphotericin B/toluene and PBC/SLE are labelled rare. (Book p722)

questions.q: All of the following are labelled RARE acquired causes of type-1 RTA EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Rare acquired causes: drugs (amphotericin B, toluene) and disease (primary biliary cirrhosis, SLE); Sjogren's is the m/c acquired cause, not rare. (Book p722)

questions.q: Inability to acidify urine in type-1 RTA is defined as urine pH greater than ______ for 3 consecutive days.
questions.exp: Urine pH > 5.5 for 3 consecutive days defines the acidification defect. (Book p722)

questions.q: The significant NAGMA of type-1 RTA corresponds to a serum HCO3- of:
questions.exp: Type-1 RTA: significant NAGMA with HCO3- 10–12 meq/L (Fanconi's milder NAGMA keeps 16–18). (Book p722)

questions.q: Calcium reabsorption from bone in type-1 RTA causes hypercalciuria with all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Hypercalciuria leads to stone formation (CaPO4), medullary nephrocalcinosis and renal rickets — not hypocalciuria. (Book p722)

questions.q: Fill up: In type-1 RTA, hypocitraturia predisposes to ______.
questions.exp: Hypocitraturia → stones; salt and water wasting → ↓ renal perfusion → secondary hyperaldosteronism → hypokalemia. (Book p722)

questions.q: All of the following are features of type-III RTA (carbonic anhydrase II defect) EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Type-III RTA (CA-II defect): osteopetrosis, mental retardation, cerebral calcification; nephrocalcinosis belongs to type-1. (Book p722)

questions.q: Match each RTA with its defect site — 1) RTA type-1 / distal 2) RTA type-2 / proximal … A) Global PCT dysfunction B) α-1 cell
questions.exp: Defect site: type-1 = α-1 cell; type-2 = global PCT dysfunction. (Book p723)

questions.q: All of the following are COMMON features shared by RTA-1 and RTA-2 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Common: inherited cause (m>F), autosomal recessive, normal RFT; phosphorus loss differs (no in type-1, significant in type-2). (Book p723)

questions.q: Match each urinary finding with the RTA type where it is significant — 1) Phosphorus loss in urine 2) Ca+ loss in urine 3) Aminoaciduria … A) RTA type-2 / proximal B) RTA type-1 / distal C) Neither type
questions.exp: Phosphorus loss and aminoaciduria are significant in type-2; Ca+ loss is significant in type-1 (absent in type-2). (Book p723)

questions.q: The bicarbonate dose required to treat RTA type-2 / proximal is:
questions.exp: Treatment HCO3-: type-1 = 2–4 meq/kg/day; type-2 = 10–15 meq/kg/day. (Book p723)

questions.q: Fill up: In the un-named cells of the CCD, the hormone acting is ADH and the channel protein is ______.
questions.exp: Un-named cells: hormone ADH, channel protein aquaporin. (Book p723)

questions.q: The functions listed for the un-named CCD cells are:
opts: Counter-current exchanger and reabsorption of free water
questions.exp: Un-named cell function: counter-current exchanger; reabsorption of free water. (Book p723)

questions.q: Fill up: The urine anion gap is calculated as Na+ + K+ − ______.
questions.exp: Na+ + K+ + UC = Cl- + UA, so Na+ + K+ − Cl- = UA − UC = urine anion gap. (Book p723)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the urine anion gap is TRUE?
opts: A positive gap favours RTA (mainly type-1) while a negative gap favours VIPoma
The gap cannot separate RTA from VIPoma
questions.exp: UAG differentiates RTA (mainly type-1) vs VIPoma: +ve → RTA, −ve → VIPoma. (Book p723)

questions.q: In the urine anion gap diagram, the unmeasured cation that falls in RTA is:
questions.exp: NH4+ is the unmeasured cation; ↓NH4+ in RTA makes the gap positive. (Book p723)

questions.q: Match each TALH transport element with its role — 1) ROM-K channel 2) ClCKB 3) Barttin 4) Claudin protein … A) Passive paracellular transport of H2O and Ca2+/Mg2+ B) Basolateral Cl- channel C) β-subunit of that Cl- channel D) Luminal K+ recycle creating electropositivity
questions.exp: ROM-K recycles K+ luminally (electropositivity); ClCKB is the basolateral Cl- channel with barttin (4) as its subunit; claudin mediates passive paracellular transport. (Book p724)

questions.q: Fill up: The basolateral Cl- channel ClCKB of the TALH requires the subunit ______.
questions.exp: ClCKB (3) pairs with barttin (4) on the basolateral side. (Book p724)

questions.q: Fill up: Passive paracellular transport in the TALH carries H2O and Ca2+/Mg2+ through the ______ protein.
questions.exp: Passive paracellular transport is via the claudin protein. (Book p724)

questions.q: Fill up: Bartter syndrome is autosomal recessive and results from a defect in the luminal ______ channel.
questions.exp: Bartter: AR, defect in the Na+-K+ 2Cl- channel of the TALH. (Book p724)

questions.q: All of the following are features of Bartter syndrome EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Bartter shows severe salt wasting, hypokalemia, alkalosis, hypercalciuria → stones, hypomagnesemia (20%) and normal to low BP — never hypertension. (Book p724)

questions.q: Match each Bartter type with its descriptor — 1) Type-I 2) Type-IV 3) Type-V … A) AD, Ca-sensing receptor defect with hypocalcemia B) m/c, children with maternal polyhydramnios C) Presents with SNHL
questions.exp: Type-I (m/c): children, maternal polyhydramnios; Type-IV: presents with SNHL; Type-V: AD, Ca-sensing receptor defect, hypocalcemia. (Book p724)

questions.q: The Bartter type labelled 'classical' that presents in adults is:
questions.exp: Type-III/classical Bartter presents in adults (types I and II in children). (Book p724)

questions.q: Indomethacin treats Bartter syndrome by:
questions.exp: Treatment: indomethacin (−) PG → blocks the prostaglandin-mediated secondary RAS activation. (Book p724)

questions.q: Fill up: The luminal entry step in the distal convoluted tubule is the Na+-______ symport.
questions.exp: DCT physiology: Na+ Cl- symport at the luminal membrane. (Book p725)

questions.q: Fill up: Gitelman's syndrome is autosomal recessive and characteristically presents in ______.
questions.exp: Gitelman: AR, adults (contrast Bartter: children). (Book p725)

questions.q: The defect in Gitelman's syndrome is in the:
opts: H+ ATPase of the α-1 cell
questions.exp: Gitelman defect: Na+-Cl- symport in the DCT. (Book p725)

questions.q: Fill up: The 100% hypomagnesemia of Gitelman syndrome follows an associated TRMP6 defect in the ______, impairing Mg2+ absorption.
questions.exp: Na+-Cl- symport defect in DCT associates with TRMP6 defect in ileum → impaired Mg2+ absorption in ileum → hypomagnesemia (100%). (Book p725)

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Gitelman's syndrome is TRUE?
opts: There is no hypocalciuria, hence no stones
questions.exp: Gitelman: no hypocalciuria (no stones), no hypermagnesemia; RFT normal. (Book p725)

questions.q: The book's note defines hypercalciuria as urinary calcium above:
questions.exp: Note: hypercalciuria → 4 mg/kg/day. (Book p725)

questions.q: Match each feature with the syndrome where it is MORE prominent — 1) Polyuria 2) Tetany 3) Urine Ca2+ … A) Gitelman syndrome B) Bartter syndrome C) Equal in both
questions.exp: Bartter: more polyuria, polydipsia, dehydration, growth retardation, urine Ca2+ and nephrocalcinosis; Gitelman: more tetany. (Book p725)

questions.q: Hypomagnesemia in Bartter syndrome is seen in:
questions.exp: Bartter: hypomagnesemia in 20% of cases (type V); Gitelman shows low magnesium in 100%. (Book p725)

questions.q: All of the following are features of Gitelman's syndrome EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Gitelman: normal RFT, mild hypokalemia/alkalosis/polyuria, failure to thrive, hypomagnesemia; nephrocalcinosis is more a Bartter feature (less in Gitelman). (Book p725)

units.title: Applied aspect: approach to renal failure

units.title: PCT transporters & phosphorus handling

units.title: Fanconi syndrome: causes

units.title: Fanconi syndrome: clinical features
units.guide: The six cardinal manifestations with their numbers (rickets, NAGMA 8–12, euglycemic glycosuria, wasting, HCO3 16–18, hypokalemia) plus the other-feature list.

units.title: CCD cell types & the P-cell
units.guide: The four CCD cell types, P-cell physiology (ENaC, AIP, ROMK/SOMK, zona glomerulosa aldosterone) and the excess-aldosterone triad leading to Conn's.

units.title: Hypoaldosteronism (RTA-IV) & renin stimulators

units.title: α-1 & β-1 cells and type-1/distal RTA
units.guide: Intercalated-cell transporters, inherited (AD/AR + SNHL) and acquired (Sjogren's m/c, rare drugs/diseases) distal RTA, its manifestations and the type-III RTA note.

units.title: RTA-1 vs RTA-2, un-named cells & urine anion gap
